relatedLinks.title: North
relatedLinks.description: North Brazil has its own geography, logistics, climate, and urban rhythm. We explain what makes the region distinctive for readers considering travel, living, or investment.
relatedLinks.image_alt: Hero image for the North page showing Teatro Amazonas in Manaus in northern Brazil.

relatedLinks.title: Northeast
relatedLinks.description: Northeast Brazil brings together strong regional identity, major coastal capitals, tourism, and very different realities between one city and another.
relatedLinks.image_alt: Hero image for the Northeast page showing Lençois Maranhenses dunes and lagoons in northeast Brazil.

relatedLinks.title: Central-West
relatedLinks.description: Central-West Brazil combines the federal capital, agribusiness influence, interior geography, and a pace of life that often surprises readers who imagine Brazil only through the coast.
relatedLinks.image_alt: Hero image for the Central-West page showing the Pantanal wetlands in central-west Brazil.

relatedLinks.title: Southeast
relatedLinks.description: Southeast Brazil concentrates business, infrastructure, and some of the country’s most diverse urban experiences. It is often the entry point for foreigners, but never a single reality.
relatedLinks.image_alt: Hero image for the Southeast page showing Rio de Janeiro, Sugarloaf Mountain, and Guanabara Bay in southeast Brazil.

relatedLinks.title: South
relatedLinks.description: South Brazil is often associated with cooler weather, mid-sized city life, and a different rhythm from tropical stereotypes. We explain what that means in practical terms.
relatedLinks.image_alt: Hero image for the South page showing the Porto Alegre skyline in southern Brazil.

relatedLinks.title: States
relatedLinks.description: State-level comparison helps readers move from country-wide fascination to more realistic shortlists. State identity affects services, culture, administration, and how cities are experienced.
relatedLinks.image_alt: Hero image for the States page showing the National Congress complex in Brasilia in central-west Brazil.
